nodes.title: Run actionlint as a declared Bazel test
nodes.summary:
The original actionlint change is fully replaced by merged import #15250 at d3f4faffa. Upstream deliberately made the Bazel actions check optional, so default lint no longer requires host Bazel. The old default-lint failure is resolved. The Make-wrapper follow-up at 8f772e58b is retired as an unnecessary request; its source, validation refs and original failed-parent evidence are preserved. It was not landed. Complete six-path replacement review and independent peer 493c0a58dbdf closed; normal exact-lease remote deletion and named local deletion are verified (receipt bffaa781a15c). Only bazel-actionlint was retired; bazel-actionlint-ci remains preserved.

The reviewed actionlint correction is integrated in public, clean and tracked MAIN 1670b46d8ba7725ee2b3c7619951e216ba53ce00. Validation continuation 3f824ddf-8b12-40b3-ae4f-8f27fc12bb63 at unchanged fork source 8f772e58b6981a9e4c8da4acedebb2b89d1812b0 runs both selected test paths uncached: the canonical Docker-builder test passes in 20 ms, and explicit DOCKER_BUILD=false passes through RBE in 98 ms. Default evidence is the actual BEP/result output without materialized XML; the RBE result has its actual Action/Command/worker/log/XML join. Sealed outcome e6382a9238e1 retains the parent FAILED after 78.680 seconds solely because default-builder shutdown returns 2; both test phases and captures succeed, and final cleanup returns zero. That contributor request is now retired because the landed optional-check contract resolves its motivating default-lint failure. This does not claim a complete public import or full-CI pass.

The authorized October 2/3 rebase is published at e89cc398592a9e40b0d876bba1d2052e045d2314 on current master b65c70734a1bc7df49d000b911848b3ad2a9cce0. The requested attributed comment to @EtiennePerot is verified at https://github.com/google/gvisor/pull/15107#issuecomment-5963408537. Current checks and feedback are recorded in the GitHub snapshot; mergeability does not establish review or CI completion. Public older-source import #15250 at 263162ee3de76a03c0cd68da9f2eba16373201fe fails Buildkite 49348: the host lint step reports that Bazel is absent from PATH. The import contains older source 6db816c6c, while the live source PR remains e89cc3985. The owning correction delegates the actions check through canonical make test, preserving the default builder route and explicit DOCKER_BUILD=false. Its narrow source/record peer passed; the proposed wrapper is preserved as historical evidence. This failure does not establish that the unrelated Podman result has the same cause. The first hosted correction validation at fork source 8f772e58b6981a9e4c8da4acedebb2b89d1812b0 fails after 1,234.198 seconds (parent 65a1d557-984f-446c-a969-4818964d9ee3, sealed outcome 33eab553e459). The canonical builder image pull and container startup succeed, and Make reaches its TEST header; no actual Bazel test result is captured before the deadline and exit 137. The explicit DOCKER_BUILD=false phase never executes. Noninteractive post-timeout inspection can run Bazel 8.3.1 in the still-running builder. Cause is unproved; the later method-only continuation removes inherited terminal input and gives collection a separate bounded deadline. The coordinator reports Linux 5.15, distinct from the observed Linux 6.1 action workers; neither is evidence of a newer worker deployment. The original public import failure and this incomplete validation remain separate.

followup.nextAction: No follow-up is requested. Preserve the reviewed optional-wrapper source and historical validation evidence.

nodes.summary:

The separate maintained artifact workflow 38107877473 finished with all seventeen non-runtime test owners passing; only clang-tidy failed on missing direct capability includes in landlock_v1.cc and proc_keys.cc. It performed no publication or deployment. Header correction 40be7e93b is public. The first focused method 6baa7930 failed on its target-file handling; corrected clang invocation eadc0591 passed both affected owners in 30.08 seconds, with all 29 source bodies and clean capture/restoration verified. Independent saved review also closes all 45 artifact-test outputs, seventeen fresh main test actions, fourteen separate XML helpers and 6,008 successful remote execution records. The original failed clang parent remains preserved. The Landlock file now exactly matches the already-published #15508 repair; no PR amendment is needed. The fork-only proc key-quota fixture has a separate root-owned extraction task, without a standalone proposal or contributor question. The separate reference-clock qualification profile originally validated source 40502e54b. Representative runtime validation 3727b648 is terminal Failed after 479.148 seconds. Clock and shared Go phases passed. The runtime phase has four passes, four sidecar-layout failures and two build failures; the analyzer phase has sixteen passes and five build failures under an accidental Werror setting. Original collection is now closed: 76 advertised output paths, 89 source bodies and 35 actual remote actions are bound. The native architecture frontend relocated do/release-smoke executables away from their gvisor-bin sidecars. Direct-rule correction 5540d55e preserves declared layout and test routing, but continuation 26d17088 failed before workload on two duplicate top-level Starlark bindings. That source-review miss and failed archive are retained. The narrow function-local correction is public at 1518c58a9. Continuation c5c00c37 passed all nine native commands, nested Docker and affected analyzers, but the full default Docker owner failed. Its actual ConnectToSelf argv contains the retired sidecar-policy warning. Five launcher injections, including Kind TOML, are removed in 05c59d539. Continuation 7c97ede0 passed all 68 unchanged Docker test and subtest identities with no skips, including ConnectToSelf and CheckpointResume, plus both owning analyzers on both CPUs. The parent/subtest hierarchy is retained rather than treating 68 names as independent bodies. All six required XML/log outputs, 93 source bodies and three fresh remote test actions are bound; successful debug references remain advertised, with forty retained originals authenticated. Product sidecar lookup and test expectations are unchanged. ConnectToSelf warning contamination is directly evidenced; the older CheckpointResume combined stream was not retained, so its warning-offset explanation is not an observed runtime cause. The separate ARM64 Actions run 38109053648 is terminal failed: three unprivileged commands passed; the root process exited zero but Bazel could not normalize its test.log ownership, so no completed root result is credited. Original collection authenticates 35 archive files and six CAS outputs; one hidden .bazelrc capture was omitted, leaving 24 of 25 expected objects. MAIN has a source-reviewed fixture correction restoring the original owners of inherited standard descriptors. Root-only ARM continuation 38109813969 passed with method 92fa3717e and public payload 5b79393b4. The actual root command retained its original 900-second deadline, reference mode and strict sidecar lookup, and Bazel completed output processing successfully. All 27 source objects and two original outputs authenticate. Its non-hidden source capture prefix closes the earlier .bazelrc omission. The previous three unprivileged passes and root NO STATUS remain separate. Actual ARM64 namespace launches remain assigned to the existing Actions route. The incompatible rootless-cgroup probe was removed from preparation without changing its nobody identity or the root-only fixture. The published mixed-unit optimization at 5b728d814 replaces four serial analyses with one loading query and one final configured analysis, and selects minimal downloads. Independent source review is complete; root owns integration and the complete unit execution. An earlier public current-upstream composition was 26643f1b6, adding the canonical NVIDIA updater’s explicit Git working directory to bb47ab2c0. That parent declares host plus both Linux Python wheel platforms on top of the generated license-catalog metadata in a647c7d6e/46dcf5b4e. The earlier 46dc revision removes one identical duplicate Moby Make recipe from 86ce3abec. Four canonical formatting/Gazelle phases passed on 86ce without generated changes in 76708ffb. License Fetch then entered Docker because the method omitted the canonical Make command-line setting. The corrected Fetch/Verify continuation 9df1de29 passed on exact 86ce in 974.285 seconds, verifying all 1,745 dependencies and 559 captured source bodies. Its only generated change updates the CodeQL vtprotobuf catalog revision and removes an unresolved colorama wheel entry, with no new license-policy exception. The exact generated output is published in a647; this does not add runtime coverage. Build-only qualification 73f96f64 is closed on 46dc: full AMD64 compilation and the public ARM64 pkg/runsc selections all passed, with all spawns remote or cached and zero runtime test actions. Canonical Nogo continuation 630b3490 is closed on the same source with 831 fresh remote analyzer tests, selecting both CPU analyses per owner. Mixed-unit Actions run 38101082599 failed during analysis on exact 46dc, with zero processes. The ARM64 coordinator created a host-only Python wheel hub, but the spelling check targets AMD64; Python 3.11 already matches. The reviewed MODULE correction preserves host tools and declares both Linux wheel platforms in both hubs. The declaration correction is public at bb47. Unchanged mixed-unit continuation 38102011573 completed with 671 of 673 owners passing and two failures. Both original ABI-parity logs report a stale NVIDIA source index: 30 versions instead of the 32 supported by current code. The first canonical updater request c6b80de9 stopped before reading tags because Git inherited bazel run’s working directory beneath an invalid generated .git marker. The public explicit-workspace correction 26643f1b6 completed 87fe4603 successfully in 1476.996 seconds. Canonical regeneration adds only two explicit unavailable-source entries, for 620.32.00 and 620.47.00; the successful public tag advertisement has neither version. All 24 public source archives are unchanged. Both CPU ABI-parity owners, updater tests and buildifier passed, and license Fetch/Verify confirms all 1,745 entries with an unchanged catalog. The exact index and unit-analysis simplification are published in bffba536e. The updater correction is also folded into the retained NVIDIA proposal at 7012ff5d9; its old source index and catalog are unchanged. The failed originals are retained. Focused Python cross-build/canonical verification 0b65f9b3 passed buildifier, the ARM64 codespell and distribution/frontend targets, and all 1,745 license checks without catalog changes. No lint is removed. On prior source 46dc, canonical Nogo is closed with 831 fresh remote tests and 30,932 spawns, none local. Broad compilation 73f96f64 finished OK in 1383.967 seconds across AMD64 all-target and ARM64 pkg/runsc phases; original artifact, source and remote-placement closure is complete. Build and analyzer results do not supply runtime or complete-profile credit for the updated source. The initial refreshed source 8e29f31e5 merged upstream 309599c1e with combined 33b622c72; its original generation request 395ec447 and subsequent failed attempts remain recorded.

Earlier combined-source evidence: The public combined candidate 33b622c72 adds the unchanged merged systrap queue-relocation and RECV ENOENT fixes to the validated routing and guest/test policies, public Gazelle lane and independent clock-readiness correction. Canonical Gazelle fix/check run 9b4d2699 succeeded on the earlier 60cce0807 composition. Its two generated BUILD attribute-order changes are applied with exact output hashes. The actual ARM64 namespace analyses succeeded with 673 owners and 694 declared shards, but the method rejected the maintained read-only info max-heap-size capture. No test ran. The corrected graph-only continuation 38097348180 at ab6f346b6 on the same payload captured both policies successfully, then failed an inline assumption that each label has one configuration. The original posix_error_test has valid ARM64 and AMD64 configurations. Saved comparison now retains all configuration/platform identities and multiplicities: both policies contain 673 labels, 674 configured owners and 694 TestRunner actions. The default namespace policy has four local actions; the empty policy has none. All eight analyses report zero processes, and both final test commands are intercepted. Independent saved review is complete. Both failed parent records remain; this is graph-only evidence for 60cce0807, not runtime or later-source coverage. The separate RC/64K graph request 1bef1c51 passed on exact source 33b622c72 with 113 authenticated files and 25 source bodies. It selects AMD64 RC 1,434 owners/2,602 actions after one explicit Nogo exclusion, ARM64 RC 919/1,775, and ARM64 64K 661/1,286. All ten analyses execute zero processes; both final test commands are intercepted. Native payload contracts and explicit TCG outer deadline/shard/argument policies verify. Independent saved review is complete. This gives no runtime, guest-boot or refreshed-8e29 credit. Its first Gazelle attempt stopped before Bazel on an untracked lockfile capture check and is retained. No latest-master merge, combined runtime pass or canonical promotion is claimed.

The complete ordinary AMD64 profile at 1146d4e23 passed through the Actions Docker bridge, with compilation remote. The separate full hosted-worker attempt, BuildBuddy 7b724cee at 1485fb247, ended failed after 374.5 seconds. Its 1,176-owner/2,138-action graph gate passed and tests actually executed remotely. Output packaging requested zip, which the lean image lacks; missing file also prevented MIME detection. The original attempt is retained. Some test bodies passed and real test failures also occurred, so packaging failure is not being treated as the sole test outcome. The same-source no-ZIP continuation, BuildBuddy 5c80f5c3, is terminal with 1,162 passing and 14 failing owners. Saved-result reconciliation binds all 4,327 selected original files and 4,276 compact-output joins. Actual XML contains 62,209 passing C++ cases, 104 failures, 2,475 skips and 24 separate wrapper entries, with no empty XML. Compared with the same-source Actions profile, 74 cases pass there but skip on RBE; two reverse skips make the net difference 72. These body-coverage gaps include Landlock ABIs, Yama, anonymous VMA names, MSG_COPY and versioned Linux behavior. They remain explicit even when their test owner passes. Optional debug URIs are retained without downloading every trace. The PTY timeout still has no proven cause. Userspace probes reproduced a missing tail after the initial read; the upstream no_room fix remains a candidate, not a deployed-kernel fact. Kprobe setup is unavailable on the actual worker kernel. The standard-receive function-trace diagnostic 2da15465 at 68edf63b08 completed all 20 original cases: 18 passed and two failed. Its complete, loss-free traces show no special-character receive callback on either failed path, while all 18 passing paths have one; receive callbacks still execute. Tty/byte identity and the exact kernel cause remain unproved. This is diagnostic evidence, not a repair or qualification pass. The current combined source 33b622c72 still reproduces the shared MONOTONIC ordering failure: a syscall read is 1,510 ns ahead of the following VDSO read. The other five actual clock cases and clang passed, and complete boot output shows no calibration reset. This is after the readiness correction and both carried systrap fixes; the cause remains unknown and it is not a worker-capability exclusion. MAIN owns the diagnosis. The authenticated failing-action VM log identifies a fresh Firecracker 1.16.2 boot with no snapshot load, so the known snapshot-offset repair does not explain this action. The general, explicit --clock-source=reference alternative is public at a1df426cd. Its first request 41f70ee8 failed before compilation or tests: the graph oracle expected 16 configured rows, but the original graph has 19 rows in 16 equivalent action-key groups. The unchanged-source continuation 9a0120e3 ran all six clock cases successfully and 480 unit cases successfully, with two configuration fixture-count failures; all seven both-CPU analyzers passed in 16 fresh actions. The fixture-only count correction is public at 0a949a24f, and restore/config continuation c1a72ebb is closed with the reference-mode checkpoint/restore evidence. The independently extracted ten-path alternative is public at 978e24600 on time-reference-clock. Its clock, unit and analyzer evidence is closed; the existing-benchmark cost comparison cf509169 executed all 52 actions on the validated qualifier, then its parent failed solely in the saved-result CPU-time parser. Saved-only correction and independent numerical review are closed. The complete clock_gettime action had a paired geometric mean duration ratio of 1.373 (95% interval 1.214–1.559), including fixed warmup and startup; self-timed guest numbers are not independent calibrated-time verification. Its first attempt d9db36f9 stopped before benchmark compilation/execution because the reused wrapper named an unavailable optional reporting tool; that failure is retained. The corrected method removes only that tool. The message-only standalone revision 684b060d4 is now awaiting an actual contributor decision; no upstream PR exists. The original pre-workload failure and partial runtime result remain preserved. This is not a provider selector or a claim about the original cause; the clock result does not establish the original cause or a performance effect. The completed discriminator 36e07999 at 5c547518a reproduced a 1,785 ns shared MONOTONIC reversal. The native and directfs owners passed, as did all six separate native handoffs. Raw-counter reversals occurred before and after the failing clock owner in the same remote action on CPUs 0 and 1. This establishes co-occurrence, not the cause or a sufficient counter-offset magnitude. The original three owners, six clock cases and 300-second limits are retained; no repair or capability exemption follows. Its bounded diagnostic b678a701 at 5f82fc46e6 reproduced both ordering violations: before shared BOOTTIME VDSO exceeded a later syscall by 13,090 ns; instrumented directfs syscall exceeded a later VDSO read by 1,722 ns. Clamp counters remained zero with no resets, so lower-bound clamping does not explain that directfs observation. The cause remains unknown and all original assertions are retained. The independent clock-readiness return correction is now awaiting contributor review at 529ae96bd; it does not explain or fix these no-reset reversals. A separate transport/affinity diagnostic d344a04a reproduced a 6,540 ns shared BOOTTIME violation in the default configuration. Both no-fast-path owners and both no-fast-path plus pinned-CPU owners passed. All 14 cases use the same binaries and original deadlines, with flags and affinity verified. Passing controls are inconclusive: transport latency may mask an error, and workers differ. The direct failed-read diagnostic 31d6bf9d passed all six runtime cases without reproducing the violation; its missing-header analyzer failure was corrected in a separate analyzer-only continuation. The cycle-event diagnostic dde26985 reproduced a 4,540 ns shared BOOTTIME reversal with one stable even parameter generation and no serialized caller-cycle regression. Its projection points to a discrepancy inside the syscall path, but Sentry cycles were not sampled in that failing run. The subsequent internal-cycle diagnostic ab045d55 passed all six cases, clang and two analyzers; 492,820 returned buffers exactly matched their syscall timespecs. Consumer continuation ce664bf9 also passed all six cases and clang: all 499,026 matched calls supplied four expected path samples, with no cycle regressions and 997,491 raw AUX changes. These instrumented runs did not reproduce the clock failure; added sampling/copy-out may affect observation. The original failure remains unresolved, with no fix or proven cross-vCPU offset. The native control 561b2c87 at 87bf6daa3 passed all three actual native cases and clang. Its two-second serialized handoff recorded 253 causal backward raw-counter transitions in 4,262,721 samples on verified guest CPUs 0 and 1. Only eight examples are retained, spanning 13–67 ticks; that is not a bound on all events. Both original native clock tests passed. This establishes a native counter-ordering anomaly on that worker/CPU pair, not the cause of the prior Sentry/VDSO failure or a repair. A separate magnitude continuation ef1b4c99 at 42c724c6e passed the same three native cases and clang. It recorded 53 backward transitions in 4,065,383 samples: 52 from CPU 0 to 1, maximum 210 ticks, and one in the reverse direction, maximum 204 ticks. Those maxima apply only to this worker/pair/run; the two runs do not establish a causal rate comparison or the Sentry failure's cause. The earlier metadata-preflight attempt executed no test processes. Its 126 original log/XML files contain 2,312 C++ passes and 54 explicit skips; all 74 previously skipped cases execute successfully. Independent saved review is complete. No new result is inferred for the 1,151 unexecuted remote owners. Its first attempt started no jobs because the concurrency key exceeded 400 characters; that literal workflow issue is corrected. No PTY or VDSO fallback, image change or blanket remote-support claim is made. Independent saved review binds all 15 jobs, 1,176 owners, 2,138 fresh test actions and 4,299 original outputs. This is bounded non-reproduction on that composition; the original ca956 timeout remains unresolved, with no causal fix or stack-capture functionality claim. These source-specific results do not establish a complete ARM64 profile pass.

The separate diagnostic d46fa9d9 completed all six isolated pipe/UDP cases successfully; its parent failed only while deleting read-only copied reports. A subsequent 60-action diagnostic c4661232 has 53 passes and seven failures: five deliberate stack-capture stops, one real TCP 120-second assertion and one warning-only runner failure. These are diagnostic results, not full-profile qualification.

The separate mixed release-candidate bucket 7, Actions 38018426239 at f311db0eb, ended in failure at 03:54 UTC. Its sole failing owner is proc/directfs on ARM64 RC, shard 2: VerifyTaskChildrenNeverReportsZeroTID continued child creation until the 300-second deadline. The root cause is unproven; no retry is claimed. This is a partial bucket, with no full-RC claim.

The complete 33-case socket-stress owner passed in Actions 38008045670 at b1b7f2549. All 33 original cases passed in uncached remote actions, with source, debug/no-strace settings and declared contracts reconciled. It keeps each case’s 3600-second deadline and debug logging, with syscall tracing disabled by default and explicitly overridable. This closes the complete stress owner under the corrected policy. It does not establish a pass for the full 661-owner ARM64 profile. The first attempt, Actions 38007298459, stopped before any build or test action because its routing hash still included the old argument list. The correction requires the new prefix and removes only that prefix from copied comparison rows; actual runtime arguments remain intact. This is fork validation infrastructure, not an upstream proposal or canonical promotion.

The three prior timeout cases passed separate untraced diagnostics on source 3cd943971. IPv4 Reset/4 passed in its one-case run. The two IPv6 cases then passed: Reset/3 in 2950.422 seconds and ShutdownCloseSecond/3 in 2245.510 seconds. Their kernel, initramfs and payload match the earlier inputs. These isolated results do not confer full-owner qualification or isolate tracing cost. The earlier 33-case run remains 30 passes and three timeouts; the preceding six-owner continuation remains five passing owners and 12 of 19 passing shards.

The original full ARM64 64K profile remains failed: 652 passing owners, seven timeouts and two failures, across 1,194 passing, fifteen timed-out and two failed shards. Independent saved review is complete. The cookie repair passed a separate complete 16-shard loopback continuation. This route uses an AMD64 OCI host and ARM64 64K Linux 6.8.0-138 guest; the native ARM64-host pilot is separate.

Closed mixed-unit evidence remains bound to e44f46dc9: all 673 selected owners and 693 original shards passed, with 675 cached remote results, fourteen fresh remote actions and four declared local ARM64 actions. Fresh outputs contain 528 passing XML entries and four explicit skips. The separate 838-target Nogo result remains bound to 7f774023a. Earlier snapshot-index loading failures and their original records remain retained.

The separate paired pipe fast-path diagnostic b871aefd at f770348a8 uses the same complete pipe owner three times per runtime setting, without test-body changes. Its five-minute capture limit provides diagnostic evidence, not qualification credit.

The retained RC kernel config confirms that legacy memory-controller support is disabled while v2 memory remains enabled. The native KillWithV1MemoryMounted fixture must check that prerequisite. The native-only absence guard is validated using the existing /proc/cgroups parser; gVisor and unexpected mount failures remain strict. The independent cgroup-controller-transfers proposal 791d920ba also restores the controller state it found and is awaiting contributor review.

The four emulation-budget adjustments are published at 12fbcc6e2e. They apply only to generated TCG variants of epoll, Unix pairs, veth and route; native/KVM deadlines, bodies, arguments and sharding are unchanged. The isolated long-running cases passed diagnostics, but those results do not qualify complete owners. The complete four-owner continuation 7919b6d2 succeeded with 11 uncached actions, including all eight Unix shards, without filters or deadline/shard overrides. Independent saved review binds all 82 archive files, 44 original outputs, 33 compact-output joins and nine captured source bodies. It confirms 828 executed C++ passes, 82 skips and two shell-wrapper passes. The longest Unix shard took 1427.497 seconds and epoll took 160.596 seconds. investigations.title: CUBIC recovery and congestion-control testing
investigations.summary: The prior single-flow high-BDP study showed higher throughput for repaired Netstack CUBIC than repaired Reno. In the separate sharing studies, Netstack received less than half the goodput against Linux, including matched Reno/Reno and CUBIC/CUBIC controls with both sender roles. The tables retain each profile, block and measurement bound. These source-specific results do not establish a universal advantage or a cause.

findings.text: Isolated production-controller regressions reproduce two recovery behaviors: after a loss reduces the congestion window from 1000 to 700, ACKs covering 700 segments over 100 ms leave it at 700 for batch sizes 1, 2 and 10. With an aged epoch, one ACK instead moves it from 700 to 776. These are controller-arithmetic observations, not an end-to-end network reproduction.

A subsequent regression through the existing TCP sender packet path completes fast recovery, then observes a congestion window of 453 before and after a full window of ACKs. It uses the existing manual clock and Pause/Resume synchronization, without sleeps, a copied CUBIC formula or new production hooks. Broader impaired-link and performance conclusions require separate evidence.

A zero-new-ACK controller regression also observes growth from 700 to 1229. The first corrective validation reported passing targeted tests and analyzers after a test-fixture correction. This does not complete the wider recovery and performance investigation.

Existing infrastructure already provides paired Linux/netstack packetdrill targets and a TCP benchmark with network namespaces, netem and iperf. This work extends those routes and the existing manual-clock packet fixtures. The original packetdrill scripts cover basic connection/close behavior; the inspected SACK/RACK recovery cases use Reno by default.

The user-approved ACK-credit repairs are now Reno PR #15576 and CUBIC PR #15579. Both include the requested got/want assertion cleanup; CUBIC also includes the reviewed arithmetic simplification. The final CUBIC check passed ten named cases on each runtime architecture and both owning analyzer targets. The 32-bit saturation argument remains a source proof, not a new 32-bit runtime result. Earlier before failures and packet evidence remain retained; no contributor question is pending for either delivered change.

All 60 planned throughput trials were retained and independently checked against their source and helper binaries. At 100 Mbps, 100 ms RTT and configured 0.1% loss, original and first-ACK-repair CUBIC had receiver-goodput medians of 7.79 and 8.59 Mbps, but paired outcomes split three wins and three losses. This does not establish an improvement. Small-BDP controls reached 19.0–19.1 Mbps. These trials exclude the later idle, epoch and listener-inheritance changes; unseeded loss and queue drops limit interpretation.

The combined CUBIC ACK-credit, idle and epoch corrections with the Reno repair passed 11 selected unit, analyzer and packet target results, including normal and race configurations. The saved evidence supports this explicit target selection; the empty case XML provides no per-case census. Correctness success does not establish a throughput advantage.

Separate fast-recovery and retransmission-timeout smoke scripts passed on native Linux 6.1 and Netstack after selecting CUBIC directly on the accepted sending socket. The earlier Netstack scripts stopped before data transfer because accepted sockets reported Reno after the listener selected CUBIC. That inheritance defect remains separate from the four passing recovery targets.

The complete 35-flow study retained five functional controls and 30 balanced 120-second comparison flows. On one worker at 100 Mbps, 100 ms RTT and configured 0.01% loss, repaired CUBIC had median receiver goodput of 36.4 Mbps versus repaired Reno at 18.8 Mbps, with CUBIC higher in all six matched blocks. Original CUBIC had median 23.15 Mbps; the repaired bundle was higher in five of six pairs. Exact source, generated inputs and runtime binaries were independently joined. This source predates utilization and retransmission-cursor repairs. Unseeded loss and queue drops limit generalization; this does not reproduce the historical outage.

Two real-packet regressions keep two packets in flight after recovery, limited separately by the application and advertised receive window. Both originally grew the congestion window from 7 to 18. The correction now passes its effective 12-target test/analyzer selection after fixing an incompletely initialized unit fixture. Both the original growth failures and the intermediate fixture failures remain recorded. This establishes the selected correctness result, without a throughput or historical-outage reproduction claim.

evidence.label: First corrected matrix (unit fixture failures retained)

findings.text: The user-approved accepted-socket inheritance repair is now PR #15574. Expected before failures and passing corrected unit, native, sandbox and analyzer targets remain recorded; the parent output-oracle failure is preserved. The user has requested maintainer review, and current-head GitHub checks and review are tracked on the PR.

Expanded RACK coverage reproduced an immediate duplicate segment after RTO with both original and corrected controllers. The sender-cursor repair passed 16 selected standalone-controller and integrated target results, including full SACK/RACK suites on both architectures, integrated TCP units, focused race tests, analyzers and formatting. Four existing RACK reorder-detection skips remain explicit. The original failures are retained. The user-approved cursor repair and independent SACK coverage are now PRs #15575 and #15577; the requested SACK arithmetic cleanup preserves the tested offsets.

evidence.label: Expanded recovery results with original failures

findings.text: The observation-harness functional check now retains per-stream receiver JSON and native ICMP observations before, during and after traffic. Five corrected client/server/both modes and the original no-probe mode passed; original startup failures remain recorded. Receiver totals and runtime helper identities were independently checked. These short checks establish instrumentation function, not comparative throughput, fairness, exact clock alignment or Netstack TCP RTT.

evidence.label: Original run with startup failures retained

findings.text: The final-controller matrix retained all 60 trials and independently joined their source, generated state, archives and actual helper binaries. At 100 Mbps, 100 ms RTT and configured 0.01% unseeded loss, repaired Netstack CUBIC exceeded repaired Netstack Reno in all six within-job pairs: median paired ratio 2.14×, range 1.62–2.36×. Repaired CUBIC also exceeded original CUBIC in all six pairs (median 1.75×), but remained below native Linux CUBIC in every pair (median 0.93×). The separate small-BDP controls are not pooled. Distinct job IDs do not establish physical-worker independence; these sequential single-flow measurements do not establish fairness, loaded latency, universal superiority or the historical outage cause.

Shared-flow functional validation is now closed. All 13 original normal modes passed, but the original expected-termination case omitted required inner cleanup records and its failed parent remains retained. A two-delimiter supervisor correction passed a normal mixed-flow control and the same termination case: both clients and flow supervisors were interrupted, both receivers were reaped, and both flow cleanups plus topology cleanup completed. Interrupted receivers do not count as completed traffic. This establishes functional capture and cleanup behavior, without a fairness, comparative-performance or precise-clock-alignment claim.

Independent review closes all 30 sharing trials and 60 raw receiver reports across three VM blocks. The original reader retained 27 observations and three analysis errors; the corrected saved-only reader preserves those 27 exactly and recovers the remaining three by bounding unlocated bytes and interval coverage. No workload was rerun. Native shared-path ICMP reports baseline median/p95 of 100 ms and loaded medians of 101–103 ms, with p95 of 105–109 ms. These are ICMP reply RTTs, not TCP RTT or pure queue delay.

All 12 matched-algorithm cross-stack trials are independently reviewed. Netstack’s share remains below half in every role-specific measurement bound, with Reno trial bounds spanning 24.0–32.8% and CUBIC bounds spanning 26.8–40.5%. These are ranges across individual observations, not pooled confidence intervals. The gap therefore persists without mixing algorithms, while its cause remains unresolved. Source inspection identified pre-existing work in disabled-probe snapshots; its performance impact has not been measured.

The original epoch qualification remains outcome unknown after its observation deadline: the service exposed no invocation or execution record and cancellation is unconfirmed. The corrected request, using exact public Git inputs instead of oversized embedded bodies, closed three expected before failures and passing full TCP unit and analyzer checks on both architectures. The epoch change is delivered as PR #15604. The separate disabled-probe comparison has completed; its source-bound interpretation remains separate from the earlier sharing studies.

In the epoch PR review, Etienne reported microbenchmark results for replacing math.Pow(t, 3) with multiplication: 13.670 to 1.912 ns and 12.625 to 1.934 ns, with 20 samples per version. The comment did not include benchmark source or environment. The user-authorized one-expression amendment is delivered at 98d5af4a3 after passing existing full TCP unit checks on AMD64 and ARM64 and the owning analyzers. The reply was posted and the thread is resolved.

The source-isolated SACK accounting study completed all 24 instrumented shared-WAN trials on three workers, with controllers and workload held fixed and four accounting production files changed. Original outputs and source joins are collected; independent result review is pending. Separately, RACK initialization checks reproduced high/wrapped-ISN failures at manual-clock time zero, with a passing low-ISN control. The correction passed eight selected targets and is delivered as PR #15618. The user-approved follow-up RTTSeq amendment is also delivered at 0a0e6fc2a, with its reply posted and thread resolved.

The sender-owner prototype passed its remote correctness checks. All eight paired WAN trials completed. Three of four Netstack-share change bounds include zero; the CUBIC-primary pair fell from 28.43–33.25% to 21.74–24.83%. These are conservative measurement bounds on one worker, not statistical confidence intervals or proof of a causal regression.

investigations.title: pkg/state: code generation and generics design
investigations.summary: Eligibility-corrected generated ordinary StateSave/Sink records at 22cf74e12 passed all 19 compatibility targets. The completed 12-pair experiment 857951e7 reports UDP Save time -10.07% and bytes -8.05%, with pointer/map/slice Save bytes and allocation counts restored to baseline. Seven control timings are nonsignificant; ControlMessage Save is -7.73% (p=.002). Independent numerical review is complete. The actual kernel pilot passed all six restore operations; this is compatibility evidence. The earlier 4e21551d7 allocation regression remains a separate cohort. Independent master correctness is closed for e3e4b2daf: eight original passing owners plus eleven corrected owners, with the original missing-dependency failure retained. Its separate twelve-pair comparison reports UDP Save -10.21% and bytes -6.27%, but pointer Save/Load regress 1.03%/3.37%. Independent numeric review is complete. UDP executable size is +5.85%, and observed UDP initialization remains 51,496 B / 98 allocations per sequence. The concrete-header follow-up is rejected as a refinement: removing the inspected interface checks did not eliminate pointer regressions and increased UDP allocated bytes relative to the generic representation. Root requested contributor review of the independent generic proposal at 7f73b15af, then held it for a newly found receiver/import name collision. FIFTH has prepared the generated StateSave spelling correction and missing regression; before/after validation f66a74d9 is active, without a result yet. No upstream PR exists, and no contributor rejection or approval is inferred.

findings.text: The current generator emits Save/Load calls with addresses of statically known fields. Sink.Save and Source.Load then accept any and reconstruct reflect.Values. The prototype will retain that known type information in generated field operations while sharing the existing wire/type/identity/wait graph. AST spelling alone is insufficient for imported, aliased or shadowed types; the generator needs a sound type proof or a compatible dynamic fallback.

At the studied Go 1.27.1 pin, the specification and compiler support generic methods. Array lengths still require constant expressions, and generic code is not automatically devirtualized. Language feasibility therefore does not establish an allocation or timing benefit.

Pointer identity, cycles, interior aliases, overlapping slices and delayed load callbacks must retain their semantics under one graph mechanism. Those requirements do not make reflective field traversal unavoidable: generated descriptors and typed operations can carry known representation information. The prototype must preserve registration before reentrant hooks and distinct aggregate storage where callbacks retain addresses; compatibility for arbitrary dynamic types remains part of the design.

The initial prototype specializes proved scalar/pointer fields and uses typed allocation and assignment while retaining the same wire and object-identity/wait graph. Pointer identity metadata still traverses the current reflective boundary. A later descriptor-based encoder could discover and snapshot objects once, then emit finalized IDs without boxing every wire value; it must cache hook/SaveValue results and captured values because callbacks and slice-tail clearing can mutate state. This is a design direction, not an executed performance result.

evidence.label: Existing object graph and struct cache

findings.text: The shared-primitive prototype at 74c23e08a passed the selected five-owner compatibility scope. In the paired study, pointer Load improved by 7.72% (p=.002); the other eight timing changes were not significant, and allocation counts did not change. Executable size still increased: UDP by 15% and state by 7.1%. CPU/heap capture and pointer-only controls have since completed. findings.text: Map reflection was the strongest measured reflection opportunity. In sampled allocation-object profiles, reflect.unsafe_New accounted for 51.12% flat in Map Load and 25.41% flat in Map Save. Map Save also spent 25.13% cumulative CPU in MapKeys and 15.24% in MapIndex; cumulative entries overlap and must not be added.

Other costs would survive simply replacing reflective field access: Stats.sample accounted for 21.24% cumulative CPU in Pointer Load, while the 32-packet UDP Save profile attributed 40.06% of sampled allocation objects to wire.Struct.Alloc and 26.53% to encodeStruct. Sample percentages are estimates, not exact allocation counts or predicted savings.

All five profiling actions completed, but the original parent failed because its collector expected a ZIP. The ten individual CPU/heap files were retained and decoded in a tool-only continuation, with no benchmark repetition. The original failed parent remains failed.

Independent saved-result review verified all 192 measured rows, 12 balanced AB/BA pairs and the actual source-to-binary inputs. Source review withdrew the first one-line decoder preallocation candidate before testing. No preallocation measurements were run; the next candidate must address the actual map-creation path.

This is a separate cohort from the earlier optional-dispatch experiment.
comparisons.note: Saved benchstat reports ±1% for both UDP time medians. Six other control timing comparisons were not significant. Pointer/map/slice Save bytes and allocation counts match baseline; control-message Save decreases from 5,624 to 5,560 B/op and from 80 to 74 allocations. UDP initialization remains 51,496 B and 98 allocations per observed sequence; initialization and executable size are outside ns/op. No process-RSS improvement is established. The nineteen-target compatibility packet retains its reader-only failed parent. The earlier experimental-dispatch checkpoint pilot supplies no runtime result for this consolidated source.

investigations.title: Scheduled tracker refresh reliability
investigations.summary: Investigate gaps in automatic GitHub status collection and publication. Keep the snapshot timestamp authoritative while determining why expected schedule events are absent.

findings.text: The active default-branch workflow is configured for minutes 18 and 48 of each UTC hour. The latest actual scheduled run was created at 01:01:30 UTC on 11 October and completed the 01:03:14 snapshot in status-only commit 560dd0edb. That newer automated snapshot was preserved before the curated update. Five earlier scheduled runs succeeded on 10 October, created at 01:18, 07:45, 13:59, 18:39 and 22:00 UTC. Successful execution is established, but the observed multi-hour gaps before event creation do not demonstrate regular 30-minute cadence. Their cause remains unexplained.

The configuration and run-history audit found no disabled workflow, wrong default branch, blocked job or queued run explaining the gap. The missing events occur before job execution, so there is no failed job log identifying their cause. No replacement scheduler or repeated re-registration has been introduced.

GitHub documents that scheduled jobs can be delayed or dropped. That is a service limitation, not proof of this gap’s cause. Manual publication through the existing collector is keeping verified snapshots visible while regular automatic cadence remains unproven.

investigations.nextStep: Continue the existing complete PR/event sweeps and inspect new schedule evidence at normal boundaries. Investigate new evidence about missing event creation; do not claim regular automatic cadence or introduce a replacement scheduler.
